- Model consistently underestimates early spikes (e.g., 47.00, 49.61) and overestimates later declines (e.g., 35.94, 33.75).
- Forecast shows upward bias in the first 10–15 days of the 30-day window, then flattens or slightly declines — true values often reverse this trend sharply.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history (e.g., 46.66 → 49.61), leading to overforecasting of subsequent values.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon — true values often drop below forecasted mean.
- Forecast lags in response to recent history: if history shows a sharp drop, model doesn’t immediately reflect it; if history shows a spike, model overreacts.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — true values show more abrupt transitions, especially in the last 5–10 days.
- Forecast assumes continuity of recent trend; true values often deviate sharply after 10–15 days, especially if recent history includes volatility or policy shifts.
